declarative.auditability_rationale: Decision is a deterministic dict lookup with the full table inspectable via policies_for(tenant_id). Compliance can reconstruct WHY in O(1) — no LLM in path.
declarative.maintainability_rationale: Compliance team edits a dict / YAML and ships. No code review needed; no engineering touch required for routine policy updates.

llm_judge.auditability_rationale: Structured JSON output gives a parseable decision + reasoning field. Compliance can audit at scale (queryable schema) but the underlying LLM remains a black box.
llm_judge.maintainability_rationale: Compliance updates the JSON policy table directly (same shape as declarative). The judge prompt is engineering-owned and rarely changes; policy table edits are low-touch.

naive_llm.auditability_rationale: Free-form LLM text reasoning is hard to align to a structured audit schema. Compliance must read prose per-decision; aggregate audits across decisions are impractical.
naive_llm.maintainability_rationale: Compliance edits an English narrative — accessible to non-engineers, but the LLM may misinterpret edits. Validation requires running the benchmark, not just reading the policy.

python_rules.auditability_rationale: Per-tenant Python callable is opaque to introspection — reasoning depends on which conditional branch fired. Decision trace requires reading code, not configuration.
python_rules.maintainability_rationale: Policy updates require an engineering touch and code review. Compliance team cannot ship a policy change on their own. Higher expressiveness ceiling, higher floor.
